sanskrit: indriyaiḥ sṛjyate yad yat tat tad vyaktam iti smṛtam avyaktam iti vijñeyaṃ liṅgagrāhyam atīndriyam
english: Whatever is produced by the senses is known as the manifest; that which is beyond the grasp of the senses and is apprehended only through its marks is to be understood as the unmanifest.

sanskrit: yathāsvaṃ grāhakāny eṣāṃ śabdādīnām imāni tu indriyāṇi yadā dehī dhārayann iha tapyate
english: These senses each grasp their respective objects — sound and the rest — and when the embodied being supports them here, he undergoes austerity.

sanskrit: loke vitatam ātmānaṃ lokaṃ cātmani paśyati parāvarajñaḥ saktaḥ san sarvabhūtāni paśyati
english: He sees the Self spread through the world and the world within the Self; the knower of the near and far, though engaged, sees all beings.

sanskrit: paśyataḥ sarvabhūtāni sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā brahmabhūtasya saṃyogo nāśubhenopapadyate
english: For one who sees all beings in all conditions at all times, who has become Brahman, no association with the inauspicious can arise.

sanskrit: jñānamūlātmakaṃ kleśam ativṛttasya mohajam loko buddhiprakāśena jñeyamārgeṇa dṛśyate
english: For one who has transcended the affliction rooted in knowledge and born of delusion, the world is seen by the light of the intellect on the path of what is to be known.

sanskrit: anādinidhanaṃ jantum ātmayoniṃ sadāvyayam anaupamyam amūrtaṃ ca bhagavān āha buddhimān tapomūlam idaṃ sarvaṃ yan māṃ viprānupṛcchasi
english: The wise Lord declared: the living being is without beginning or end, self-originated, eternally imperishable, incomparable, and formless — all this that you, O brahmin, ask me about has its root in austerity.

sanskrit: indriyāṇy eva tat sarvaṃ yat svarganarakāv ubhau nigṛhītavisṛṣṭāni svargāya narakāya ca
english: The senses are indeed everything — both heaven and hell; when restrained they lead to heaven, when let loose they lead to hell.

sanskrit: eṣa yogavidhiḥ kṛtsno yāvad indriyadhāraṇam etan mūlaṃ hi tapasaḥ kṛtsnasya narakasya ca
english: The entire discipline of yoga consists in the restraint of the senses; this is indeed the root of all austerity and likewise the root of all hell.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena doṣam ṛcchaty asaṃśayam saṃniyamya tu tāny eva tataḥ siddhim avāpnute
english: Through indulgence of the senses one falls into fault without doubt; by restraining those same senses, one thereafter attains perfection.

sanskrit: ṣaṇṇām ātmani nityānām aiśvaryaṃ yo 'dhigacchati na sa pāpaiḥ kuto 'narthair yujyate vijitendriyaḥ
english: One who achieves mastery over the six ever-present senses within the self — that conqueror of the senses is not bound by sins, still less by misfortunes.

sanskrit: rathaḥ śarīraṃ puruṣasya dṛṣṭam; ātmā niyantendriyāṇy āhur aśvān tair apramattaḥ kuśalī sadaśvair; dāntaiḥ sukhaṃ yāti rathīva dhīraḥ
english: The body of a person is seen as a chariot; they say the Self is the driver and the senses are the horses — the skilled one, vigilant with well-trained and disciplined horses, travels comfortably like a wise charioteer.

sanskrit: ṣaṇṇām ātmani nityānām indriyāṇāṃ pramāthinām yo dhīro dhārayed raśmīn sa syāt paramasārathiḥ
english: The steadfast one who holds the reins of the six ever-present and turbulent senses within the self would be the supreme charioteer.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ prasṛṣṭānāṃ hayānām iva vartmasu dhṛtiṃ kurvīta sārathye dhṛtyā tāni jayed dhruvam
english: For senses let loose on their tracks like horses, one should exercise steadiness in charioteering; by steadiness one will certainly conquer them.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yan mano 'nuvidhīyate tad asya harate buddhiṃ nāvaṃ vāyur ivāmbhasi
english: When the mind follows along with the roving senses, it carries away one's intellect as the wind carries away a boat upon the waters.

sanskrit: yeṣu vipratipadyante ṣaṭsu mohāt phalāgame teṣv adhyavasitādhyāyī vindate dhyānajaṃ phalam
english: One who is resolute and studious in those six matters wherein people go astray from delusion when fruits arrive — that one obtains the fruit born of meditation.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evaṃ tu sūkṣme kathite dharmavyādhena bhārata brāhmaṇaḥ sa punaḥ sūkṣmaṃ papraccha susamāhitaḥ
english: Markandeya said: O Bharata, when the Dharma-Hunter had thus spoken on subtle matters, that brahmin, with concentrated mind, asked once more about something subtle.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca sattvasya rajasaś caiva tamasaś ca yathātatham guṇāṃs tattvena me brūhi yathāvad iha pṛcchataḥ
english: The brahmin said: Tell me accurately and in truth about the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas as they truly are, explaining them correctly to me as I ask here.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi eṣāṃ guṇān pṛthaktvena nibodha gadato mama
english: The hunter said: Come, I shall tell you what you ask of me — know the qualities of these separately as I speak.

sanskrit: mohātmakaṃ tamas teṣāṃ raja eṣāṃ pravartakam prakāśabahulatvāc ca sattvaṃ jyāya ihocyate
english: Among these, tamas is characterized by delusion and rajas by agitation; sattva, because it is abundant in luminosity, is called the highest here.

sanskrit: avidyābahulo mūḍhaḥ svapnaśīlo vicetanaḥ durdṛśīkas tamodhvastaḥ sakrodhas tāmaso 'lasaḥ
english: Abounding in ignorance, bewildered, prone to sleep, unconscious, dim-sighted, overwhelmed by darkness, wrathful, and slothful — such is the tamasic person.

sanskrit: pravṛttavākyo mantrī ca yo 'nurāgy abhyasūyakaḥ vivitsamāno viprarṣe stabdho mānī sa rājasaḥ
english: One who is verbose, scheming, attached, envious, inquisitive, O seer among brahmins, arrogant and proud — such is the rajasic person.

sanskrit: prakāśabahulo dhīro nirvivitso 'nasūyakaḥ akrodhano naro dhīmān dāntaś caiva sa sāttvikaḥ
english: Abounding in luminosity, steadfast, without excessive curiosity, free from envy, not given to anger, wise and self-restrained — such a person is sattvic.

sanskrit: sāttvikas tv atha saṃbuddho lokavṛttena kliśyate yadā budhyati boddhavyaṃ lokavṛttaṃ jugupsate
english: But when the sattvic person, being fully awakened, is troubled by worldly conduct and comes to understand what is to be understood, he turns away in disgust from worldly behavior.

sanskrit: vairāgyasya hi rūpaṃ tu pūrvam eva pravartate mṛdur bhavaty ahaṃkāraḥ prasīdaty ārjavaṃ ca yat
english: For the form of dispassion arises first; the ego-sense becomes soft, and whatever straightforwardness there is becomes serene.

sanskrit: tato 'sya sarvadvaṃdvāni praśāmyanti parasparam na cāsya saṃyamo nāma kva cid bhavati kaś cana
english: Thereafter all the pairs of opposites within him mutually subside; and no restraint whatsoever is needed for him anywhere.

sanskrit: śūdrayonau hi jātasya sadguṇān upatiṣṭhataḥ vaiśyatvaṃ bhavati brahman kṣatriyatvaṃ tathaiva ca
english: For one born in the womb of a shudra who abides in good qualities, O brahmin, the state of a vaishya arises, and likewise the state of a kshatriya.

sanskrit: ārjave vartamānasya brāhmaṇyam abhijāyate guṇās te kīrtitāḥ sarve kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: For one who lives in straightforwardness, brahminhood arises. All those qualities have been described — what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca pārthivaṃ dhātum āsādya śārīro 'gniḥ kathaṃ bhavet avakāśaviśeṣeṇa kathaṃ vartayate 'nilaḥ
english: The brahmin said: When the bodily fire meets the earthly element, how does it exist? And how does the wind function through the particular cavities of the body?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca praśnam etaṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇena yudhiṣṭhira vyādhaḥ sa kathayām āsa brāhmaṇāya mahātmane
english: Markandeya said: O Yudhishthira, this question raised by the brahmin — the hunter expounded it to that great-souled brahmin.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca mūrdhānam āśrito vahniḥ śarīraṃ paripālayan prāṇo mūrdhani cāgnau ca vartamāno viceṣṭate bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca sarvaṃ prāṇe pratiṣṭhitam
english: The hunter said: The fire, taking up residence in the head, protects the body; the vital breath, operating in both the head and the fire, stirs into action — all that has been, all that is, and all that shall be is established in the vital breath.

sanskrit: śreṣṭhaṃ tad eva bhūtānāṃ brahmajyotir upāsmahe sa jantuḥ sarvabhūtātmā puruṣaḥ sa sanātanaḥ mano buddhir ahaṃkāro bhūtānāṃ viṣayaś ca saḥ
english: That very one is the best among beings — we worship the light of Brahman; that living being is the Self of all beings, the eternal Person; mind, intellect, ego-sense, and the objects of beings — he is all that.

sanskrit: evaṃ tv iha sa sarvatra prāṇena paripālyate pṛṣṭhatas tu samānena svāṃ svāṃ gatim upāśritaḥ
english: Thus here he is everywhere sustained by the vital breath; behind it, the equalized breath, each taking up its own course.

sanskrit: bastimūle gude caiva pāvakaḥ samupāśritaḥ vahan mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ cāpy apānaḥ parivartate
english: At the base of the bladder and in the rectum, the fire takes up residence; the downward breath, carrying urine and feces, moves in rotation.

sanskrit: prayatne karmaṇi bale ya ekas triṣu vartate udāna iti taṃ prāhur adhyātmaviduṣo janāḥ
english: That one breath which operates in the three — in effort, action, and strength — those who know the inner self call it the udana breath.

sanskrit: saṃdhau saṃdhau saṃniviṣṭaḥ sarveṣv api tathānilaḥ śarīreṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ vyāna ity upadiṣyate
english: The breath lodged in every joint throughout the body of human beings is designated the vyana breath.

sanskrit: dhātuṣv agnis tu vitataḥ sa tu vāyusamīritaḥ rasān dhātūṃś ca doṣāṃś ca vartayan paridhāvati
english: The fire spread through the bodily elements, stirred by the wind, runs throughout, processing the essences, the elements, and the humors.

sanskrit: prāṇānāṃ saṃnipātāt tu saṃnipātaḥ prajāyate ūṣmā cāgnir iti jñeyo yo 'nnaṃ pacati dehinām
english: Through the confluence of the vital breaths, their joint action arises; the heat, which is to be known as the fire, digests the food of the embodied beings.

sanskrit: apānodānayor madhye prāṇavyānau samāhitau samanvitas tv adhiṣṭhānaṃ samyak pacati pāvakaḥ
english: The prana and vyana breaths, concentrated between the apana and udana, together with them at their station, cause the fire to digest properly.

sanskrit: tasyāpi pāyuparyantas tathā syād gudasaṃjñitaḥ srotāṃsi tasmāj jāyante sarvaprāṇeṣu dehinām
english: And its extent reaches to the anus, which is thus called the guda; from that arise the channels in all the vital breaths of the embodied.

sanskrit: agnivegavahaḥ prāṇo gudānte pratihanyate sa ūrdhvam āgamya punaḥ samutkṣipati pāvakam
english: The vital breath that carries the force of fire is repelled at the end of the rectum; coming upward again, it once more projects the fire upward.

sanskrit: pakvāśayas tv adho nābhyā ūrdhvam āmāśayaḥ sthitaḥ nābhimadhye śarīrasya prāṇāḥ sarve pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: The stomach of cooked food lies below the navel; above it stands the stomach of raw food; in the center of the navel, all the vital breaths are established.

sanskrit: pravṛttā hṛdayāt sarvās tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā vahanty annarasān nāḍyo daśa prāṇapracoditāḥ
english: All ten channels, flowing from the heart sideways, upward, and downward, carry the essences of food, impelled by the vital breaths.

sanskrit: yoginām eṣa mārgas tu yena gacchanti tatparam jitaklamāsanā dhīrā mūrdhany ātmānam ādadhuḥ evaṃ sarveṣu vitatau prāṇāpānau hi dehiṣu
english: This is the path of yogins by which they reach the Supreme — the steadfast ones who have mastered the posture of exhaustion place the Self in the crown of the head. Thus the prana and apana breaths are spread through all embodied beings.

sanskrit: ekādaśavikārātmā kalāsaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtaḥ mūrtimantaṃ hi taṃ viddhi nityaṃ karmajitātmakam
english: Know that which has eleven modifications as its nature and is assembled from an accumulation of fractions — know it as the embodied one, eternally characterized by a self won through action.

sanskrit: tasmin yaḥ saṃsthito hy agnir nityaṃ sthālyām ivāhitaḥ ātmānaṃ taṃ vijānīhi nityaṃ yogajitātmakam
english: The fire that is ever established in that one, placed as if in a cooking vessel — know that Self as eternally characterized by a self won through yoga.

sanskrit: devo yaḥ saṃsthitas tasminn abbindur iva puṣkare kṣetrajñaṃ taṃ vijānīhi nityaṃ tyāgajitātmakam
english: The divine one who is established in that, like a drop of water on a lotus — know that knower of the field as eternally characterized by a self won through renunciation.

sanskrit: jīvātmakāni jānīhi rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamas tathā jīvam ātmaguṇaṃ viddhi tathātmānaṃ parātmakam
english: Know rajas, sattva, and tamas as belonging to the individual soul; know the individual soul as the quality of the self, and know the self as partaking of the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: sacetanaṃ jīvaguṇaṃ vadanti; sa ceṣṭate ceṣṭayate ca sarvam tataḥ paraṃ kṣetravido vadanti; prākalpayad yo bhuvanāni sapta
english: They call the quality of the individual soul conscious; it acts and causes everything to act. Beyond that, the knowers of the field declare: the one who fashioned the seven worlds.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu bhūtātmā na prakāśate dṛśyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā jñānavedibhiḥ
english: Thus the Self of beings does not manifest in all beings; yet it is seen by those who know knowledge, through a subtle, penetrating intellect.

sanskrit: cittasya hi prasādena hanti karma śubhāśubham prasannātmātmani sthitvā sukham ānantyam aśnute
english: Through the serenity of the mind one destroys both good and evil karma; with a serene self, established in the Self, one experiences happiness and eternity.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇaṃ tu prasādasya yathā tṛptaḥ sukhaṃ svapet nivāte vā yathā dīpo dīpyet kuśaladīpitaḥ
english: The mark of serenity is this: as a satisfied person sleeps pleasantly, or as a lamp kindled by a skilled hand burns in a windless place.

sanskrit: pūrvarātre pare caiva yuñjānaḥ satataṃ manaḥ laghvāhāro viśuddhātmā paśyann ātmānam ātmani
english: Constantly yoking the mind in the early and late watches of the night, eating lightly, with a purified soul, seeing the Self through the Self—

sanskrit: pradīpteneva dīpena manodīpena paśyati dṛṣṭvātmānaṃ nirātmānaṃ tadā sa tu vimucyate
english: —he sees with the lamp of the mind, as with a lit lamp; having seen the Self as free from self, he is then liberated.

sanskrit: sarvopāyais tu lobhasya krodhasya ca vinigrahaḥ etat pavitraṃ yajñānāṃ tapo vai saṃkramo mataḥ
english: By all means, the restraint of greed and anger — this is considered the most purifying of sacrifices; austerity is indeed the crossing over.

sanskrit: nityaṃ krodhāt tapo rakṣec chriyaṃ rakṣeta matsarāt vidyāṃ mānāpamānābhyām ātmānaṃ tu pramādataḥ
english: Always protect austerity from anger, protect prosperity from envy, protect knowledge from honor and dishonor, and protect the self from heedlessness.

sanskrit: ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmaḥ kṣamā ca paramaṃ balam ātmajñānaṃ paraṃ jñānaṃ paraṃ satyavrataṃ vratam
english: Non-cruelty is the supreme dharma; forgiveness is the supreme strength; self-knowledge is the supreme knowledge; the vow of truth is the supreme vow.

sanskrit: satyasya vacanaṃ śreyaḥ satyaṃ jñānaṃ hitaṃ bhavet yad bhūtahitam atyantaṃ tad vai satyaṃ paraṃ matam
english: The utterance of truth is better; truth as knowledge brings welfare; that which is supremely beneficial to all beings — that is considered the highest truth.

sanskrit: yasya sarve samārambhāḥ nirāśīrbandhanāḥ sadā tyāge yasya hutaṃ sarvaṃ sa tyāgī sa ca buddhimān
english: One for whom all undertakings are always free from the bonds of desire, one for whom everything is offered in renunciation — that one is a true renunciant and truly wise.

sanskrit: yato na gurur apy enaṃ cyāvayed upapādayan taṃ vidyād brahmaṇo yogaṃ viyogaṃ yogasaṃjñitam
english: That from which not even a guru could dislodge him through instruction — know that as union with Brahman, separation called union.

sanskrit: na hiṃsyāt sarvabhūtāni maitrāyaṇagataś caret nedaṃ jīvitam āsādya vairaṃ kurvīta kena cit
english: One should not harm any beings; one should conduct oneself in friendliness and equanimity; having obtained this life, one should not make enmity with anyone.

sanskrit: ākiṃcanyaṃ susaṃtoṣo nirāśitvam acāpalam etad eva paraṃ jñānaṃ sadātmajñānam uttamam
english: Possessionlessness, perfect contentment, freedom from craving, and steadiness — this alone is supreme knowledge; self-knowledge is ever the highest.

sanskrit: parigrahaṃ parityajya bhava buddhyā yatavrataḥ aśokaṃ sthānam ātiṣṭhen niścalaṃ pretya ceha ca
english: Abandoning acquisition, be disciplined in vow through the intellect; attain the sorrowless state, the immovable, both in the next world and in this.

sanskrit: taponityena dāntena muninā saṃyatātmanā ajitaṃ jetukāmena bhāvyaṃ saṅgeṣv asaṅginā
english: One who desires to conquer what is unconquered must be a sage constant in austerity, self-restrained, with a controlled soul, unattached amid attachments.

sanskrit: guṇāguṇam anāsaṅgam ekakāryam anantaram etad brāhmaṇa te vṛttam āhur ekapadaṃ sukham
english: Quality and the absence of quality, non-attachment, single-pointed action without interruption — this conduct of yours, O brahmin, they call the one step of happiness.

sanskrit: parityajati yo duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ cāpy ubhayaṃ naraḥ brahma prāpnoti so 'tyantam asaṅgena ca gacchati
english: The person who renounces both sorrow and happiness attains Brahman utterly and proceeds through non-attachment.

sanskrit: yathāśrutam idaṃ sarvaṃ samāsena dvijottama etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotum icchasi
english: All this, O best of twice-born, has been told to you in brief as I have heard it. Everything has been declared to you — what more do you wish to hear?

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca evaṃ saṃkathite kṛtsne mokṣadharme yudhiṣṭhira dṛḍhaṃ prītamanā vipro dharmavyādham uvāca ha
english: Markandeya said: O Yudhishthira, when the entire teaching on the dharma of liberation had thus been spoken, the brahmin, with a heart firmly pleased, then addressed the Dharma-Hunter.

sanskrit: nyāyayuktam idaṃ sarvaṃ bhavatā parikīrtitam na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid dharmeṣv iha hi dṛśyate
english: All of this proclaimed by you is endowed with right reasoning; nothing whatsoever in the matters of dharma here appears to be unknown to you.

sanskrit: vyādha uvāca pratyakṣaṃ mama yo dharmas taṃ paśya dvijasattama yena siddhir iyaṃ prāptā mayā brāhmaṇapuṃgava
english: The hunter said: See, O best of twice-born, the dharma that is manifest in me — the dharma by which I, O chief among brahmins, have attained this perfection.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha bhagavan kṣipraṃ praviśyābhyantaraṃ gṛham draṣṭum arhasi dharmajña mātaraṃ pitaraṃ ca me
english: Rise quickly, O revered one, and enter within the house — you, who know dharma, deserve to see my mother and father.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ity uktaḥ sa praviśyātha dadarśa paramārcitam saudhaṃ hṛdyaṃ catuḥśālam atīva ca manoharam
english: Markandeya said: Thus addressed, he entered, and saw a mansion supremely adorned, charming, with four halls, and exceedingly beautiful to the heart.

sanskrit: devatāgṛhasaṃkāśaṃ daivataiś ca supūjitam śayanāsanasaṃbādhaṃ gandhaiś ca paramair yutam
english: It resembled the abode of the gods, was well-honored by divine beings, crowded with beds and seats, and filled with the finest fragrances.

sanskrit: tatra śuklāmbaradharau pitarāv asya pūjitau kṛtāhārau sutuṣṭau tāv upaviṣṭau varāsane dharmavyādhas tu tau dṛṣṭvā pādeṣu śirasāpatat
english: There, dressed in white garments, his parents were honored, having been fed and utterly content, seated on excellent chairs — and the Dharma-Hunter, seeing them, prostrated his head at their feet.

sanskrit: vṛddhāv ūcatuḥ uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha dharmajña dharmas tvām abhirakṣatu prītau svas tava śaucena dīrgham āyur avāpnuhi satputreṇa tvayā putra nityakālaṃ supūjitau
english: The two elders said: Rise, rise, O knower of dharma — may dharma protect you; we are pleased; obtain long life through your purity. Son, you have always honored us well, with you as a true son.

sanskrit: na te 'nyad daivataṃ kiṃ cid daivateṣv api vartate prayatatvād dvijātīnāṃ damenāsi samanvitaḥ
english: You have no other deity — not even among the gods; through your diligence in serving the twice-born, you are endowed with self-restraint.

sanskrit: pituḥ pitāmahā ye ca tathaiva prapitāmahāḥ prītās te satataṃ putra damenāvāṃ ca pūjayā
english: Your father's fathers and likewise their fathers too — they are always pleased with you, son, through your self-restraint and your reverence for us.

sanskrit: manasā karmaṇā vācā śuśrūṣā naiva hīyate na cānyā vitathā buddhir dṛśyate sāṃprataṃ tava
english: Your service in mind, action, and speech is never found wanting; nor is any other erroneous understanding seen in you at present.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa yathā vṛddhau supūjitau tathā tvayā kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ tadviśiṣṭaṃ ca putraka
english: As the two elders were well honored by Rama the son of Jamadagni, so have you done everything — and even more than that, dear son.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tatas taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tābhyāṃ dharmavyādho nyavedayat tau svāgatena taṃ vipram arcayām āsatus tadā
english: Markandeya said: Then the Dharma-Hunter introduced that brahmin to the two of them; and the two welcomed that brahmin and honored him with a proper greeting.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tāṃ pūjāṃ dvijaḥ papraccha tāv ubhau saputrābhyāṃ sabhṛtyābhyāṃ kaccid vāṃ kuśalaṃ gṛhe anāmayaṃ ca vāṃ kaccit sadaiveha śarīrayoḥ
english: Having received that honor, the twice-born asked the two of them, along with their son and their servants: Is all well in your household? And are your two bodies always free from affliction here?
